subject: Math
text_verbatim: Chapter 1 Numberland Adventures: Up to 999 The single digits are named: 1 One 2 Two 3 Three 4 Four 5 Five 6 Six 7 Seven 8 Eight 9 Nine Numbers from 11 to 19 are called teen numbers. When we say these numbers, we can hear 'teen' in 11 Eleven 12 Twelve 13 Thir-teen 14 Four-teen 15 Fif-teen 16 Six-teen 17 Seven-teen 18 Eigh-teen 19 Nine-teen most of them: thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen. Even though eleven and twelve sound different, they are also teen numbers because they come between 10 and 20. 5

illustrations.description: A yellow poster framed in dark brown, titled implicitly by the preceding line 'The single digits are named:'. Contains a 3x3 grid of purple crown-shaped badges, each badge showing a white digit (1-9) and, beside each badge, the digit's name written in purple text: 1/One, 2/Two, 3/Three, 4/Four, 5/Five, 6/Six, 7/Seven, 8/Eight, 9/Nine.
illustrations.pedagogical_role: reference chart mapping single digits 1-9 to their number-word names
illustrations.text_in_image: 1 One, 2 Two, 3 Three, 4 Four, 5 Five, 6 Six, 7 Seven, 8 Eight, 9 Nine
illustrations.count_method: grid is a fixed 3x3 layout with each cell's digit printed as its own answer key (not an ambiguous tally); verified by reading the 9 printed digit labels directly, cross-checked against the 3x3 grid structure, counted twice

illustrations.description: A dark-green chalkboard poster framed in dark brown, with a 3x3 grid of numbered price-tag/ticket shapes in teal (for 11, 12) and yellow (for 13-19), each showing a black digit (11-19) and, beside it, the number's name in white chalk-style text, with the '-teen' suffix hyphenated for 13-19 (e.g. 'Thir-teen', 'Four-teen') to highlight the shared 'teen' sound.
illustrations.pedagogical_role: reference chart mapping teen numbers 11-19 to their number-word names, visually emphasising the shared '-teen' suffix via hyphenation
